minutes.headline: Most hearings continued to Sept. 17 for missing erosion-control details; three compliance certificates approved.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission held three new and two continued wetlands hearings, continuing nearly all of them to September 17 so applicants could add erosion controls, trench/pipe details, or a tree-removal diagram to their plans. A tree-removal determination at 44 Hemlock Terrace was approved with a 2:1 replacement condition, three certificates of compliance were approved, and the commission agreed to enforce its existing 7-day deadline for late supplemental filings.

what_happened.line: Most wetlands hearings, including a solar array, a driveway/water line, and a common driveway, were continued to September 17 for missing erosion-control and other plan details.
The commission approved continued review of tree removal at 44 Hemlock Terrace, permitting up to 20 trees down under a 2:1 replacement condition, with a diagram due next meeting.
A demolition and two-unit dwelling application at 68A Laurel Lane was approved after an initial vote failed for lack of quorum and the full record was re-presented.
Three certificates of compliance were approved, for 701 Reservoir Road, 6 Peninsula Drive, and 828 Lancaster Avenue.
The commission agreed to enforce its existing rule requiring supplemental filings at least seven days before a scheduled hearing.

why_it_matters: Property owners with pending applications at 560 Mulpus Road, 809 Chase Road, and 1083 Northfield Road will not get a final decision until the September 17 hearing.
The tree-replacement condition at 44 Hemlock Terrace is the kind of standard the commission can apply to future tree-removal requests.
Enforcing the seven-day filing deadline could push other applicants' hearings to a later date if their paperwork arrives late.
